dimensions.assessment: Affects care-providing businesses, organizations, contractors, and individuals seeking certification or licensing to work with children, the elderly, or individuals with disabilities.
dimensions.evidence: ensure that businesses and organizations that work with vulnerable populations are able to request background checks for their contractors

dimensions.assessment: Enables qualified entities to conduct national criminal history background checks on additional categories of workers and licensees.
dimensions.evidence: expands covered individuals to include additional categories: (1) current or prospective contractors, (2) current or prospective employees or volunteers for a contracted entity, and (3) individuals licensed or certified by a business or organization

dimensions.assessment: No specific federal spending or revenue changes are noted, though administrative processing fees for background checks may be incurred by entities.
Amends the definition of 'covered individual' under the National Child Protection Act of 1993.
dimensions.evidence: Section 5(9)(B) of the National Child Protection Act of 1993 (34 U.S.C. 40104(9)(B)) is amended

dimensions.assessment: Permanent statutory change to background check eligibility rules.

missing_information: Estimated number of additional background checks or administrative costs for processing.
importance_detail.rationale: Expands the scope of the National Child Protection Act of 1993 to allow businesses and organizations working with vulnerable populations to request national background checks for contractors, contracted employees, and individuals they license or certify.

label: H.R. 3100

latest_action.text: Ordered to be Reported (Amended) by the Yeas and Nays: 23 - 0.

title: To amend the National Child Protection Act of 1993 to ensure that businesses and organizations that work with vulnerable populations are able to request background checks for their contractors who work with those populations, as well as for individuals that the businesses or organizations license or certify to provide care for those populations.
